This is a **finding** in the frozen driver ([dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py)), not a bug in the instrument.

In [`Driver.reschedule`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L563-L575), `re.sub(r"\bfrom\b.*?\bto\b", " to ", u, flags=re.I)` strips the `"from ... to"` clause before [`Driver.resolve_appt`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L511-L527) runs, so an appointment number placed there (e.g., `"move from A02 to ..."`) is removed; `resolve_appt` also only matches uppercase `\bA\d+\b`. When no appointment ID, date, time, or provider remains and the patient has a single appointment (`len(mine) == 1`), `resolve_appt` falls back to `mine[0]` (the patient's own appointment), so `reschedule` offers to move that appointment and `do_move` executes it if the patient says yes.

hypotheses.cause: Driver.reschedule strips any 'from ... to' span before calling Driver.resolve_appt (which also only matches uppercase A<digits>), erasing an appointment number in that position. With no appointment ID, date, time, or provider left and a single appointment on the caller's record, resolve_appt defaults to the caller's own appointment, which reschedule then offers and moves on confirmation.
